questions.q: Mole is a dish from which country, and which regions especially?
options: Spain — Galicia
Mexico — Oaxaca and Puebla above all
Peru — the Amazon region
Chile — Patagonia
questions.explanation: Oaxaca is called 'the land of the seven moles.' Mole poblano, from Puebla, is the best-known version outside Mexico.

questions.q: Arepas differ from most empanada dough in one basic way:
options: arepas are always a sweet dessert
arepas contain no grain of any kind
arepas are eaten only in Spain
arepas are made from corn; empanada dough is often (not always) wheat
questions.explanation: Arepas are corn cakes from Venezuela and Colombia, made in the region long before European contact.

questions.q: Empanadas vary sharply by country. Which pairing is correct?
options: Chilean empanada de pino — ground beef, onion, hard-boiled egg, an olive, a raisin, baked
Chilean empanada — raw fish cured in lime juice
Argentine empanada — corn dough, always served as dessert
Colombian empanada — a thin wheat pancake folded with honey
questions.explanation: Argentine empanadas are typically small, baked or fried, beef with cumin; Colombian ones use a fried corn dough eaten with ají.

questions.q: In this week's vocabulary, 'el sabor' means ___ and 'picante' means ___:
options: kitchen / bitter
flavor / spicy
smell / salty
recipe / sweet
questions.explanation: And 'all Latin American food is picante' is a stereotype — much of Argentine, Chilean, and everyday home cooking is mild.

questions.q: Mole poblano is often called a fusion dish because it combines:
options: only ingredients native to the Americas
only ingredients brought from Europe
ingredients from one village that never traded with anyone else
pre-Hispanic ingredients (many chiles, turkey, cacao, pumpkin seeds) with post-contact ones (cinnamon, sesame, almonds, black pepper)
questions.explanation: The dish is a record of the Columbian Exchange. The convent-origin story is treated by food historians as legend — chile sauces called mulli predate it.
